The Sinking of a Malibu Megaproject
 
Plus, the making of one of America’s priciest compounds and a historic Newport Beach home built for a famed naturopath
 
By Kerry Barger
 
 
The Case earlier this month. ADAM AMENGUAL
 

This is an edition of the WSJ Homes newsletter, a weekly guide to luxurious properties, celebrity homes, interior design and the housing market. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here.

 

Another Los Angeles spec-home builder may have flown too close to the sun.

 

Scott Gillen’s decadelong vision for the Case—a cluster of five midcentury-inspired mansions overlooking the Malibu coastline—is unraveling. Entities tied to the 66-year-old developer filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection over the summer. He’s also battling a partner in bankruptcy court over control of the project, which aimed to bring in nearly a half a billion dollars in sales to ultrawealthy buyers. Only one of the five homes has sold.

 

Gillen is hardly the first spec builder to run aground. Nile Niami’s Bel-Air megamansion, the One, was undone by massive cost overruns and delays that forced it in into foreclosure. Once listed for $500 million, the home was auctioned off for $126 million in 2022.

 

“There are developers who fall in love with their own product,” said agent Josh Altman, former star of “Million Dollar Listing Los Angeles,” who briefly listed a property for Gillen years ago. “When they stop making it about dollars and cents and start thinking their work is uniquely special, that’s where they get in trouble.”

 
 
Scott Gillen is pictured in 2018. MICHAL CZERWONKA FOR WSJ
 

Who paid $311 million for nearly 19 acres of prime waterfront property in Naples, Fla.? That question has circulated ever since a mystery billionaire paid $225 million for an estate there last year, then dropped another $86 million on the property next door.

 

The buying spree created one of America’s most expensive residential compounds, putting the buyer in rarefied company with Jeff Bezos and Ken Griffin. The secretive assemblage also highlights the massive wealth pouring into Naples, a market long overshadowed by Palm Beach and other ultraluxury enclaves.

 

Finally, we go inside a historic Newport Beach, Calif., home created for famed naturopath Philip Lovell. The home originally had sleeping porches in lieu of bedrooms, allowing for as much outdoor time as possible.

Inside the $311 Million Land Grab to Create One of America’s Priciest Homes

 
 
NAPLESKENNY PHOTOGRAPHY
 

A mystery billionaire bought 19 acres in prime Naples. Local real-estate agents say it’s a harbinger of things to come for the Florida coastal city.

 
 
 

What’s the Deal?

 
 
1 OAK STUDIOS/ONE SOTHEBY’S INTERNATIONAL REALTY
 

New York Knicks star Josh Hart and his wife, Shannon Hart, are putting their getaway in Pinecrest, Fla., back on the market for $5.699 million.

 

Minecraft creator Markus Persson is listing his Beverly Hills mansion for $70 million, the same price he paid when he outbid Jay-Z and Beyoncé for the home.

 

An oceanfront Palm Beach estate is in contract to be sold for about $160 million. If it closes, the deal would be one of the priciest ever in the elite Florida enclave.

 

Want to see more deals? Sign up for our Mansion Deals email alert to have the biggest and best luxury home sales and listings delivered to your inbox.

 
 
 

The Luxe Life

 
 
STERLING REED
 

Fresh air, nude sunbathing and a raw vegetarian diet: that was Philip M. Lovell’s prescription for Angelenos. For his own family, the naturopath commissioned a California home that eliminated bedrooms.

 

Christopher Lloyd got his first taste of acting in elementary school after a magician invited him onstage. “I was in on the trick, I was funny and 400 kids reacted. I was hooked.”
